title: Establishing a phosphoproteome for ovarian carcinoma histotypes
projectDescription: Ovarian cancer is the eight most common cancer in the women and the deadliest gynecologic malignancy. The majority of patients (90%) are diagnosed with epithelial ovarian cancer (EOC), which is comprised by five main histotypes – high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma (HGSC), low-grade serous ovarian carcinoma (LGSC), endometrioid ovarian carcinoma (EC), mucinous ovarian carcinoma (MC), and clear cell ovarian carcinoma (CCC). The established diagnostic biomarker CA-125 is unspecific and has been shown to not be suitable for early detection. Due to limited diagnostic tools and EOC being asymptomatic in early stages (I-II), 70% of patients are diagnosed in late stages (III-IV) and therefore the disease is associated with poor prognosis. Although the histotypes have distinct clinicopathologic characteristics, first line treatment has remained the same the last four decades regardless of histotype. In this study, we aimed to profile the phosphorylated proteins of primary tumors from a cohort of 180 EOC patients comprising HGSC, EC, MC, and CCC across all stages.
sampleProcessingProtocol: Primary tumor tissue was homogenized in 2% sodium dodecyl sulfate and 50 mM triethylammonium bicarbonate (TEAB) using a Covaris ML230 ultrasonicator, and protein content was determined with bicinchronic acid (BCA) using the Pierce BCA Protein Assay Kit (ThermoFisher Scientific). A total of 150 µg protein per sample was used for reduction and alkylation in 150 µL lysis buffer composed of 100 mM TEAB and 2% SDS by incubating for 15 min at 95 °C. Protein aggregation capture and enzymatic digestion was performed on MagReSyn Hydroxyl beads (Resyn Biosciences) using Lys-C (1:500, w/w, Thermo Fisher) and trypsin (1:250, w/w, Promega), automated on a KingFisher™ Flex system. Peptides were washed with 0.1% TFA. After digestion, peptides were eluted with 60% acetonitrile, 5% TFA and 0.1 M glycolic acid. Phosphopeptides were enriched on MagReSyn Zr-IMAC HP beads (Resyn Biosciences) in a 2:1 bead-to-peptide ratio, using a binding solvent containing 100% acetonitrile, 5% TFA, and 0.1 M glycolic acid and two washing steps with acetonitrile and TFA. Phosphopeptides were eluted with 1% aqueous ammonia (pH 10-11). LC-MS/MS was performed on an Evosep One LC system (Whisper zoom mode 40SPD, 32-minute gradient) coupled to a Thermo Q Exactive HF-X Orbitrap mass spectrometer, acquiring data in DIA mode using Xcalibur. Full MS scans were acquired at a resolution of 120,000 over an m/z range of 350–1400, with an AGC target of 3 × 10⁶ and a maximum injection time of 25 ms. MS2 scans were recorded at 15,000 resolution using 50 staggered DIA windows of 13.7 m/z, with normalized collision energy (NCE) set to 27.
dataProcessingProtocol: Mass spectra were searched against a reviewed human FASTA database (Swissprot, 20504 entries, February 2025) and common contaminants (cRAP) using DIA-NN (v. 2.2.0), where the entries were used to generate an in-silico spectral library with precursor charge states 1-4 between 460-1160 m/z. Peptidoform scoring was enabled, and intensities were normalized with RT-dependent cross-run normalization. Match between runs (MBR) was enabled. Maximum number of missed cleavages was set to 1. Fixed carbamidomethylation of cysteins, N-terminal excision of methionine, and a maximum of 2 variable phosphorylations of STY per peptide was set as modifications. Full settings can be found in the DIA-NN log file.
